title: Musicians move west; nights at Jack's Basket Room
summary: The war brought musicians west, Leonard Feather arrived, and he lists the all-star nights at Jack's Basket Room.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And things were just really happening. During that time, the War was in the Pacific, and all of the people in the nation were moving West, you know, because all the guys were leaving, going moving, so everything was moving this way. The writers were the ones late getting here. Leonard Feather is about the only writer out of the East that came out here during that period. I met him when I was working at the Streets of Paris in 1945, his first time out here, you know. They were a little late getting out here. A lot of things were going on out here, but they were still stuck there in New York, you know, where the business was done.

And a lot of things happened that really should have been covered during that period, a lot of great events. I will always remember some of the nights at Jack's Basket Room, where we had Morris Lane and Lucky Thompson, Sonny Criss, Willie Wells, just a whole slew of them...there was Wardell Gray, Dexter... Just all on the bandstand, all through. Lawrence Marable was just getting himself together on the drums; and Chuck Thompson, a very fine drummer, was on the scene at that time; and Roy Porter; and a fine piano
piano player named Charlie Fox, out of St. Louis, was around here during that time, and Jimmy Bunn, the pianist; and Billy Hadnott, bass; Red Callender, bass.
Erroll Garner formed a trio later with Harold "Doc" West and Red Callender and him, and I was on some sets with them.
